title: What Double Encryption does, when to use it and what it costs
aliases: additional layer of encryption inside the outer TLS tunnels

prose.label: Where it is off.
prose.text: {{browser-access-default-off}} {{extranet-unsupported}} The combinations the console refuses are in [[zpa.app-segments.settings]].

default-tls-and-in-memory.statement: By default, traffic between Zscaler Client Connector and an App Connector is encrypted using TLS 1.2 tunnels between Client Connector and the Public or Private Service Edge, and between the App Connector and the Service Edge; standard Private Access application traffic is not encrypted by Zscaler as it transits the Service Edge in memory and is never written to disk. Enabling double encryption when defining an application adds a layer of encryption inside the outer TLS tunnels, so that traffic is encrypted in memory as it transits the Service Edge.

quotes: By default, traffic between Zscaler Client Connector and an App Connector is encrypted using TLS 1.2 tunnels between Zscaler Client Connector and the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA), and between the App Connector and the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge.
However, standard Private Access application traffic is not encrypted by Zscaler as it transits the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge in memory, and is never written to disk.

Enabling double encryption when defining an application allows an organization to add an additional layer of encryption inside the outer TLS tunnels, so that traffic is encrypted in memory as it transits the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge.

mechanism.statement: When double encryption is enabled on an application segment, traffic for applications matching that segment is encrypted using Client Connector and App Connector certificates signed by the intermediate signing certificates, and is sent to the Service Edges through TLS sessions initially set up between Client Connector and the App Connector.

quotes: When double encryption is enabled on a specific application segment, traffic for the application matching that application segment is encrypted using Zscaler Client Connector and App Connector certificates signed by the intermediate signing certificates.
This encrypted traffic is sent to the Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges through TLS sessions that are initially set up between the Zscaler Client Connector and the App Connector.

when-to-use.statement: Double encryption is recommended only for sensitive data transmitted over unencrypted protocols such as HTTP, FTP or telnet, and is not needed for end-to-end encrypted protocols such as HTTPS, SSH or RDP; using it for end-to-end protocols is strongly discouraged because it gives three layers of encryption, an unnecessary performance cost and possible MTU issues.

quotes: Double encryption is recommended only for sensitive data transmitted over unencrypted protocols (e.g., HTTP, FTP, telnet, etc.).

You do not need double encryption for applications that leverage end-to-end encrypted protocols (e.g., HTTPS, SSH, RDP, etc.) because the content of that traffic is already protected by the protocol's encryption.

Use of double encryption for end-to-end protocols is strongly discouraged, since you end up with three layers of encryption (outer TLS encryption, inner double encryption, native protocol encryption) which incurs unnecessary performance cost and can cause MTU issues.

connector-capacity.statement: Enabling double encryption requires additional App Connector processing; typically the traffic counts double against the App Connector's capacity compared with standard Private Access traffic, so 100 Mbps of double encryption traffic has the same performance cost as 200 Mbps of standard application traffic.

quotes: If you enable double encryption, additional processing by the App Connector is required.
Typically, this means the traffic counts double against the App Connector's capacity, versus standard Private Access traffic.
For example, 100 Mbps of double encryption traffic has the same performance cost on the App Connector as 200 Mbps of standard application traffic.

shared-ca.statement: To enable double encryption on relevant applications, the certificates used to sign the connector and client certificates must share a certificate authority, either the default CA created within Private Access at provisioning time or a custom PKI CA from the customer, so default-provisioned tenants can use it simply by enabling it; double encryption fails if the client and App Connector certificates do not share a common root CA.

quotes: To enable double encryption on relevant applications, the certificates used to sign the connector and client certificates must share a certificate authority (CA).
The CA can be either the default CA that was created within Private Access at the provisioning time, or it can be a custom public key infrastructure (PKI) CA from the customer
the default-provisioned tenants can use double encryption simply by enabling it, as the certificates adhere to the requirements stated above
Double encryption fails if the certificate of a client and a certificate of an App Connector do not share a common root CA.

fqdn-level.statement: Double encryption occurs at the FQDN level: if it is enabled for an application segment containing an FQDN, all application segments sharing that FQDN have double encryption enabled. In the page's example, a segment app1.company.com on TCP port 80 with double encryption on means a different segment with the same FQDN on TCP port 22 also has it on.

quotes: Double encryption occurs at the FQDN level.
If double encryption is enabled for an application segment containing a FQDN, then all application segments sharing that FQDN will have double encryption enabled.

For example, if there is an application segment labeled app1.company.com TCP port 80 with double encryption turned on, then a different segment with the same FQDN (e.g., app1.company.com TCP port 22) will also have double encryption turned on.

browser-access-default-off.statement: By default, if a Browser Access-enabled application was defined, Double Encryption is disabled.

quotes: By default, if a Browser Access-enabled application was defined, Double Encryption is disabled.

extranet-unsupported.statement: Double encryption is associated with the data traffic over an App Connector; because extranet does not use a traditional App Connector, double encryption is not supported for it.

quotes: Double encryption is associated with the data traffic over an App Connector. Because extranet doesn't use a traditional App Connector, double encryption is not supported for it.

fqdn-spread-visibility.title: How the FQDN-level spread of Double Encryption shows on the other segments
fqdn-spread-visibility.detail: The Understanding Double Encryption page says all segments sharing the FQDN have double encryption enabled. It does not say whether the other segments show the console flag or `doubleEncrypt` as enabled, or whether disabling it on one segment disables it on the others.
